EER for pregnancy aged 19–50 years
1st trimester: adult EER þ 0 energy expended in pregnancy þ 0 energy deposition
2nd trimester: adult EER þ 160 kcal/day energy expended in pregnancy þ 180 kcal/day energy deposition
3rd trimester: adult EER þ 272 kcal/day energy expended in pregnancy þ 180 kcal/day energy deposition
EER for lactation aged 19–50 years
0–6 months: adult EER þ 500 kcal/day milk energy  170 kcal/day body fat loss
6–12 months: adult EER þ 400 kcal/day milk energy  0 kcal/day body fat loss

which different tissues metabolize fuel. This is controlled in part by the circulating concentration of thyroid hormones. Adults with
an above-average level of circulating thyroid hormones tend to have a higher but still normal BMR. Smokers’ BMRs are approxi-
mately 5% above normal, perhaps because of activation of the sympathetic nervous system.
Young women show a swing in BMR that is at its lowest in the late follicular phase of the menstrual cycle, just before ovulation.
On ovulation, the basal body temperature rises rapidly by approximately 0.5 C and the BMR immediately increases but rises
